diagnosed_failures: A fixed 145 N.s threshold entered ragdoll before attempting support recovery. Ordinary contacts now use residual momentum, support margin, corrective movement and delayed failure; F9 is explicitly a deliberate fall.

The first reduced controller still fell too easily in some directions at 190 N.s. Eight-direction tests exposed this; the unrestrained step allowance was adjusted and all eight now recover, while 350 N.s still fails after 290 ms.

The first partner escape turned its root instantly, rotating the anchored shirt away from the hand and dropping a grip after 20 ms. Partner turning now has a rate limit and walking cadence follows escape speed; the final hold is tested separately from a successful native ball recovery, which correctly changes LT back to protection.

The initial stronger mass model partly canceled its visible torso reaction. Disturbance lean now follows initial momentum while corrective support and damping recover the pose; F8 is tested against ordinary idle motion.

Cloth previously reconstructed world velocity and capped it below sprint speed. It now transports with the animated skin and integrates relative velocity, with damped inertia and interpolated anchors; the zero-timestep interpolation case is covered.

The late-header regression exposed a stationary aerial command drifting into an interception gait and losing standing-header eligibility. Buffered stationary aerial preparation now waits on the reception axis; original reach and skin contact gates remain unchanged.

A focused 7 m/s transport test exposed a 0.0989 m tracking-joint error. Kinematic roots now advance over both half-steps instead of reporting double speed followed by zero; the final error is recorded by sprint_joint_error_m.

Concurrent render output could split PLAYER_MATCH_FRAME JSON between printf calls. Match records now use a single stdio call; the complete rendered match regression is rerun without discarding malformed records.
The first-person camera used world-up eye displacement and a second position filter. It now uses the rendered head transform and an outside-body camera sphere plus rendered skin-distance checks.
limitations: Native root and legs remain animated. The disturbance controller is capture-point inspired, not IHMC QP control, a learned muscle policy, or a full shared 22-player rigid-body simulation.

The 288 runtime references are procedural variants from 18 native sources including mirrors. Eight manually digitized 2D keyposes from one CC0 kicking sequence are an illustrative motion study, not new 3D capture or hundreds of independent rotoscoped plays.
The OpenCV pose-model download was denied with HTTP 403 by both consulted hosts, so automatic video-to-3D inference was not run.
Contextual LT gripping, scripted escape and the additional shirt constraint are implemented in the training partner laboratory; the full match retains native CPU and tackles.
The shirt remains a bounded low-resolution XPBD shell on 16 movable torso vertices of the existing character. There is no detailed sleeve folding, tearing, or general garment self-collision.
Arm and body collision envelopes are approximations. They do not guarantee zero triangle intersection for all poses, players and obstacles.
First-person clearance was measured at recorded rendered samples; the test is not a guarantee for every possible camera and body configuration.
The existing intermittent Chest_Run scenario remains documented in docs/player-match-validation.json and is not claimed solved by this revision.
All rendered checks use Linux and an SDL virtual Xbox controller. Windows was crosscompiled and the portable package verified; its GUI and a physical controller were not tested here.
